clue.text: Strong point in favour of long hair

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: An argument about the best thing to be said for growing your hair long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong point' reads as a merit in an argument, but it is a defensive stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified building is literally a strongly defended position, a military stronghold.

clue.text: Tart about travel, showing bottle

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the next

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A traveller's tart carries a bottle with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' could suggest a person; it is pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A large vessel with a handle and spout for wine or ale is a kind of bottle or jug.

clue.text: Detail military personnel mention

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to cite is to mention

explanation.surface: An order to assign soldiers to a commendation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail' looks like the army word for assigning soldiers, but it means list item by item. RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To list or enumerate facts one by one is to recount them aloud in order, which matches giving particulars.

clue.text: Social reformer making a variety of babyfood popular

parts.note: a rusk is a hard biscuit given to teething babies
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A campaigner wins fame by popularising a baby food.
explanation.walkthrough: John Ruskin was the Victorian art critic and social thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ruskin wrote and campaigned against industrial conditions, promoting education and workers' welfare in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Concealing and disguising things more

indicators.note: to disguise something is to alter its appearance, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters of things and more rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hides and camouflages ever more objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering something completely so it cannot be seen, as in stifling a yawn, is hiding it.

clue.text: A crawler falls back before royalty

indicators.note: going back means these letters are written in the opposite direction

parts.note: to dip is to fall or drop
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A grovelling courtier retreats in a bow before the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A crawler sounds like a toady at court; here it is a creature that crawls. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: This eight-legged creature creeps along walls and floors, so it is fairly described as something that creeps about.

clue.text: Valued before many acknowledgements of indebtedness

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
an IOU is a written note admitting a debt

explanation.surface: Something prized before a heap of debt notes piled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured and of great worth is dear to its owner, highly prized and cherished.

clue.text: Joint veto resolution taken in parliament

indicators.note: taken in means held inside another word
a resolution breaks something down and settles it anew, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: the letters of veto rearranged
the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A joint resolution against a veto is passed in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' and 'resolution' sound like parliamentary language, but the definition is a woodworking joint. The Dáil is the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is an interlocking woodwork joint of flared tenons that fit into matching slots.

clue.text: Not settled, so not given support

parts.note: a rest is a support, as an armrest
less means without, lacking

explanation.surface: Someone unsettled because nobody backed them.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'not given support' as support followed by a word meaning without.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidgety and unable to relax or stay still describes someone uneasy and agitated.

clue.text: An odd escort for an older member of the family!

definitions.text: an older member of the family

indicators.note: something odd is strange or irregular, so the letters of the next word are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
the six letters of escort rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange choice of companion to accompany an elderly relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from whom one is descended, a family member from an earlier generation.

clue.text: Gets out the greenstuff

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the green foliage of plants

explanation.surface: Someone clears away the vegetables or the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greenstuff' hints at cash or vegetables, but it is foliage on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means departs, and the plural noun names the flat green parts growing on plants and trees.

clue.text: Striking the Conservatives as comprehensive

parts.note: workers out are on strike
the Conservatives are the political right

explanation.surface: A picture of a sweeping walkout by the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: An outright victory is total and complete, leaving nothing out, so the adjective means thorough and complete.

clue.text: A reporter playing a Shakespearean role

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gun, which makes a report, a bang, when fired
second meaning: the swaggering companion of Falstaff in Henry IV, Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: A journalist takes to the stage in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: A report is the bang of a gun, so a firearm is a reporter. The same name belongs to Falstaff's braggart crony.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun produces a report when fired, and Ancient Pistol is a comic character in several Shakespeare history plays.

clue.text: Cut the string and share out fairly

parts.note: a lace is a string or cord, as for a shoe
to ration is to allocate fair portions

explanation.surface: Instructions to snip a cord and divide something evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb in the instructions; it is a noun meaning a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep jagged tear in the skin or flesh is a wound, the noun sense of a gash.

clue.text: Rues a failure in efforts to make lots of money

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the next word
a failure is something that has gone wrong, so the preceding letters come out in a broken order

parts.note: the letters of rues and a, rearranged
tries are attempts or efforts

explanation.surface: Someone regrets failing in their attempts to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rues a failure' reads as regret over a flop; 'a failure' is the anagram signal working on 'Rues a', and the result goes inside TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasuries are stores of wealth or funds, so the plural noun loosely stands for large sums of cash.

clue.text: Following decline, a European intended to raise the standard

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the answer is for; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: following sets one word after the other in the order given

parts.note: to flag is to weaken or decline
a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: After a slump, a European official means to improve quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise the standard' sounds like improving quality, but a standard is a flag to hoist.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall mast is the upright from which a banner is hoisted, so it exists for lifting colours.

clue.text: Wanting more than some, nevertheless

parts.note: to be after something is to want it
all is more than some

explanation.surface: A greedy person wants more than a share, regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in spite of everything, despite what was expected, which is the sense of however.

clue.text: Getting awfully stern after tea, they'll give voice

indicators.note: awfully means in a dreadful way, so the next word is mangled
after places one piece behind the other in the given order

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
the letters of stern rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone turns very strict after the tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha, or char, is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Singers who intone psalms or liturgy in a monotone are people who sing out with their voices.

clue.text: Not operating in the right way

definitions.text: Not operating in the right way

parts.words: Not operating in the right way
parts.note: surface reading: working incorrectly or improperly
setter's reading: not using the right hand, so favouring the other one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like 'correct', but it is the side: someone who works with the other hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who naturally uses the left hand for writing and tasks does not work with the right hand.

clue.text: The guy from down under responsible for the spadework

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Australian slang for a mate or fellow Australian
second meaning: one who digs with a spade

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' is Australia; the word was a nickname for Australian soldiers and a friendly term for a fellow there.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an Australian chap in slang, and literally names whoever turns soil with a spade.

clue.text: Get into trouble over a glass of sherry

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the next

parts.note: to cop it is British slang for being punished or in trouble
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets told off for having a sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: To cop it is British slang for getting into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A copita is the narrow tulip-shaped Spanish glass from which fino sherry is traditionally drunk.

clue.text: View round about noon undisturbed

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word goes around what follows

parts.note: to see is to view
re means about, concerning
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A peaceful view around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and tranquil, untroubled by agitation, describes a peaceful state of mind or scene.

clue.text: He wrote "The Environmentalist Direction"

parts.note: an environmentalist is a Green
E for east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: An author is credited with a book titled The Environmentalist Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a book title; it is wordplay. Graham Greene was the English novelist of Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was a celebrated twentieth-century English novelist, so he is someone who wrote books.

clue.text: A singer, a Brit, unhappily single

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things going badly, so the preceding letters are disturbed

parts.note: the letters of a and brit rearranged
single means one

explanation.surface: A lonely, unhappy British vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice between tenor and bass names the performer who sings in that range.

clue.text: Some people put on a gerrymandering ass

parts.note: surface padding, giving no letters

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across put on a gerrymandering

explanation.surface: Voters fall for a fool who rigs electoral boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ass' reads as an insult for the gerrymanderer, but it is the animal. Gerrymandering is redrawing voting districts for party advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild donkey of Asia, a species of the ass family.

clue.text: Desiring change of place to get the best view

definitions.note: the answer is the place that gives the view

indicators.note: a change of place moves the letters around into new positions

parts.note: the eight letters of desiring rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants to move seats so they can see better.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats right beside the boxing ring are where spectators see the action most closely and clearly.

clue.text: Leaderless men have an inclination to join up

indicators.note: without a leader means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a ship that lists leans, has an inclination

explanation.surface: Men without a commander feel like signing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for military service is to join the armed forces, as recruits do.

clue.text: Extension in credit facility provision

parts.note: taken as written
CR is the abbreviation for credit
facility can mean ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: A bank extends a customer's credit line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provision' adds nothing to the letters; it rounds off the banking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlargement or rise in size or amount is a growth, which is what extending something achieves.
